newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Motoring legends team up on motorcycles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Motoring legends team up on motorcycles.

text.p: Two of the motoring world's legendary names, Porsche AG and Harley-Davidson Inc, are teaming up to make motorcycle engine parts, the German car maker said on Wednesday.
Porsche said each company would contribute $10 million to the project in which the U.S. motorcycle maker would hold a 51 percent stake and Porsche 49 percent .
Production of the parts, to be used in new model Harley-Davidson motorcycles, is to take place in the U.S. and should begin within a couple of years, Porsche said.
A spokesman for the German company said it had wanted to team up with a motorcycle maker for some time and the deal with Harley presented "a very interesting opportunity."
The pact helps fulfil Porsche's desire to reduce its dependence on the fickle market for sports cars and ties it to one of the best-known motorcycle makers in the world.
According to a report in "Manager Magazin", the production plant would be built in Kansas City in the U.S. in 1999 but a Porsche spokesman would not confirm such a plan.
Porsche will be responsible for organisation of the joint venture and motor development, the magazine said.
